title: The A₅ Simplicity Proof Chain
description: Exposes the complete proof chain from A₅ simplicity to the Abel-Ruffini theorem: A₅ is simple → Sₙ (n≥5) not solvable → general quintic unsolvable by radicals. Fully verified with 0 sorries and 0 axioms.

references.citation: Abel, N.H., Mémoire sur les équations algébriques, où l'on démontre l'impossibilité de la résolution de l'équation générale du cinquième degré (1824).

overview.historicalContext: Abel proved in 1824 that the general quintic has no radical solution. Galois later (1832) gave the complete characterization: a polynomial is solvable by radicals iff its Galois group is solvable. The key group-theoretic fact is that A₅ is the first non-abelian simple group, making S₅ the first non-solvable symmetric group.
overview.problemStatement: Expose the proof chain from A₅ simplicity to Abel-Ruffini with each step named and documented.
overview.proofStrategy: Use Mathlib's alternatingGroup.isSimpleGroup_five and Equiv.Perm.not_solvable, wrapping them in named theorems with pedagogical documentation.
keyInsights: A₅ (order 60) is the smallest non-abelian simple group — this single fact drives everything
The derived series gets stuck: [A₅, A₅] = A₅ because A₅ is simple and non-abelian
The threshold is exact: S₄ solvable (derived series terminates) but S₅ not solvable
